fact: The Central Bank of Sudan says it licenses electronic payment system services providers, and it revoked Al-Asjad's licence on review by a technical and legal committee.
Sudan Horizon reports Bede Sudan launched its BBAN wallet service after receiving approval from the Central Bank of Sudan.

The Central Bank of Sudan announced revocation of Al-Asjad's licence to provide electronic payment system services, and says licences are conditional on continuing compliance with its published standards and need its written approval for integration.
CBOS Circular 7/2026 says mobile-payment financial institutions hold a CBOS licence under the 2020 regulation, and CBOS approves every USSD financial service before launch and supervises it.

EBS general manager Saif Barri says EBS operates Sudan's national payments infrastructure under Central Bank of Sudan supervision, including the national switch that connects all Sudanese banks and settlement with the central bank.
